summary.text: A 45-year-old woman, previously in good health, presented to the emergency department with myalgia, asthenia and a temperature of 37.4 °C. Oxygen saturation was 98% and all laboratory results were normal. SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR on a nasal swab was positive and she had a mild form of COVID-19 pneumonia.

On admission an unenhanced chest CT showed multiple rounded peripheral ground-glass opacities, especially in the right lower lobe. She was isolated and received symptomatic and antibiotic treatment without needing oxygen, and was discharged after 4 weeks when completely asymptomatic with two consecutive negative respiratory samples.
A repeat chest CT showed complete reabsorption of the GGOs with no lung abnormalities. The pneumonia had resolved clinically and she was completely asymptomatic at the follow-up CT.

summary.text: A 64-year-old man with no other comorbidities presented after five days of fever and recent onset dyspnea. He had tachypnea, a temperature of 39 °C and coarse breath sounds at admission, with oxygen saturation 98%. Neutrophil count and CRP and LDH were elevated, lymphocyte count was low, and SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR on a nasal swab was positive.

Admission chest CT showed bilateral extensive GGOs and consolidations with prevalent peripheral distribution in the upper and lower lobes. He was isolated, received symptomatic and antibiotic treatment without needing oxygen, and was discharged after 4 weeks when asymptomatic with two consecutive negative respiratory samples.

A repeat chest CT showed persistent diffuse interlobular septal thickening with fibrotic appearance and an air bubble sign with bronchiectasis, although the pneumonia had resolved clinically and he was completely asymptomatic at the follow-up CT.
